sentences: Top sports and wildlife photography shooters, this one is for you.
Today, Nikon announced a new telephoto lens that focuses on getting you close to the action: the NIKKOR Z 120-300mm f/2.8 TC VR S.
There are cool tools, and then there are professional precision tools that don’t cut any corners in giving you the highest level of optical performance a brand can offer.
The NIKKOR Z 120-300mm f/2.8 TC VR S promises to be this lens for professional sports and wildlife photographers.
A fast telephoto full frame pro-level zoom lens in the company’s S-Line, the lens covers a focal length range of 120mm to 300mm with a fast f/2.8 aperture throughout the zoom range.
But it has another trick up its sleeve.
This is also the world’s first f/2.8 zoom to feature a built-in 1.4× teleconverter.
So, quickly needing to adjust to cover athletes at greater distances is as simple as the flip of a switch.

With the teleconverter activated, the lens's reach extends to a super-telephoto focal length of 420mm at the long end while still remaining relatively light at 6 lbs (2,735 g), making it about 1.1 lbs (515 g) lighter than the previous F-mount version from 2020.
The lens is top of the line and priced accordingly.
Nikon says that it will be available in mid-November 2026 for a suggested retail price of $13,999.95.
So, for my sports shooters out there, what do you think?
Is this destined to be the newest addition to your kit?
I was hoping that it would be lighter.
If you have a 70-200mm, which is amazing and light, how much would this lens at this weight and price be helpful?
70-200, 600mm, perhaps 180-600 and where would this fit in at that price?
Maybe for sports but less likely with wildlife.
